UK.treaty_note: UK is a structural outlier: 0% statutory withholding on ordinary dividends for foreign holders, with no treaty needed because there is nothing to relieve.
UK.reclaim_difficulty: none — no withholding is applied at source, so there is nothing to reclaim
UK.confidence: High — well-established, widely-cited fact per the source's Confidence Ratings section

Germany.treaty_note: US treaty reduces statutory to ~15% for portfolio (non-controlling) holdings, ~5% for qualifying corporate holdings ≥10%. The reduced rate is not automatic — it depends on a treaty existing (it does, for a US investor), the investor's account structure supporting relief-at-source or after-the-fact reclaim, and correct paperwork.
Germany.reclaim_difficulty: moderate — reclaiming the ~11-point gap between statutory and treaty rate requires an active Steuerbescheinigung certificate process; free if using a German broker with relief-at-source, costly/cumbersome otherwise
Germany.confidence: Medium — directionally solid, corroborated by tax-summary-style sources, but exact current-year rate should be re-verified before being hard-coded (per source's Confidence Ratings)

France.statutory_rate: 25% (post various reforms — source explicitly flags this as needing re-verification of the current-year PFU rate)
France.treaty_note: US treaty reduces statutory to ~15% for portfolio holders. Reclaim requires country-specific forms (historically styled e.g. "5000/5001" or "2777") filed via the paying agent/custodian bank.
France.reclaim_difficulty: moderate-to-high — real cost and friction reported by practitioners for the reclaim process
France.confidence: Low on the exact current statutory PFU rate (explicitly listed in the source's Open Questions as needing re-verification); Medium on the general shape (statutory ~25%, treaty ~15%)

Switzerland.statutory_rate: 35% — one of the highest in the developed world
Switzerland.treaty_note: US treaty reduces statutory to as low as 15% (portfolio holdings) or 5% (qualifying ≥10% corporate holdings). The ~20-point gap between statutory and treaty rate must be ACTIVELY reclaimed if relief-at-source is not available through the custodian.
Switzerland.reclaim_difficulty: high — document-heavy (apostille/certification requirements, multi-language forms), widely reported as one of the more onerous reclaim processes in Europe; Switzerland is the textbook 'notoriously bad' jurisdiction for withholding drag absent relief-at-source
Switzerland.confidence: High on the 35% statutory rate and the high-friction reclaim process (corroborated by multiple sources including Swiss-specific tax-focused sites, per the source's Confidence Ratings); Medium on the exact treaty-reduced rates

Japan.treaty_note: US treaty reduces to 10% (portfolio holdings) / 5% (≥10% holdings) — a moderate drag relative to Switzerland/Germany/France.
Japan.reclaim_difficulty: low-to-moderate — relief-at-source is reasonably well supported by major global custodians
Japan.confidence: Medium — directionally solid but exact current-year rate should be re-verified before being hard-coded

Australia.statutory_rate: ~30% statutory on UNFRANKED dividends only; franked dividends carry NO withholding tax at all
Australia.treaty_note: Australia's dividend imputation ("franking credit") system means many Australian dividends are partly or fully 'franked' — statutory withholding does not apply to the franked portion of a dividend at all. Franking credits themselves are largely NOT usable by non-resident/foreign investors (they are a domestic Australian tax offset). US treaty reduces the unfranked-dividend rate to ~15% for portfolio holders.
Australia.reclaim_difficulty: low for franked dividends (nothing withheld to reclaim); standard treaty-relief process for the unfranked portion
Australia.confidence: High on the franking mechanism itself and its exemption of the franked portion from further withholding, and on franking credits not being usable by foreign holders (standard, well-documented feature of Australian tax law per the source's Confidence Ratings); Medium on the exact unfranked statutory/treaty percentages
Australia.franking_warning: CRITICAL, non-obvious trap explicitly flagged by the source: headline 'dividend yield' is NOT a reliable proxy for after-withholding-tax yield in Australia the way it might be elsewhere, because the same company can pay partially franked dividends that vary by payment. A screen must know whether a given ASX distribution is franked/unfranked to correctly model after-tax yield; a conservative default (assume partial/no franking) is a reasonable simplification absent per-distribution data.

Canada.treaty_note: US treaty reduces statutory to 15% for portfolio US holders.
Canada.confidence: Medium — directionally solid but exact current-year rate should be re-verified before being hard-coded

China.reclaim_difficulty: unresolved — genuinely complex and access-route-dependent per the source; flagged for deeper, instrument-specific research if a China-domiciled name enters the candidate set, rather than a single blended assumption
China.confidence: Low on the effective rate for any specific access route (explicitly flagged in the source's Open Questions as unresolved); Medium on the 10% treaty-text figure itself

Taiwan.statutory_rate: ~21% for non-resident individuals on dividends (historical figure — source explicitly flags this exact percentage as needing current-rate verification)
Taiwan.treaty_note: STRUCTURAL TRAP: the US has NO income tax treaty with Taiwan at all (a diplomatic-status-driven structural gap). A US investor holding Taiwanese equities directly is exposed to the FULL statutory Taiwanese withholding rate with NO treaty relief available whatsoever — a meaningfully worse outcome than most other major APAC markets. Taiwan is often lumped in with 'developed APAC' in coverage terms but sits in a structurally worse withholding-tax position than Japan, Korea, or Australia purely because of a treaty-network gap, not tax policy per se.
Taiwan.reclaim_difficulty: not applicable — there is no treaty to reclaim against; the full statutory rate is the final, unrelievable outcome
Taiwan.confidence: High on the absence of a US-Taiwan tax treaty (durable, well-established structural/diplomatic fact per the source's Confidence Ratings); Medium on the exact ~21% statutory percentage (explicitly flagged as needing re-verification)
